transcript:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortega (Redwood SE), Lina Cho (Redwood SE), Sara Lin (Empiric Finance - Head of ML), Tom Berger (Empiric Finance - CTO), Priya Menon (Empiric - Infra Lead), Alex Ruiz (Empiric - Sec Ops)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on Dedicated capacity — reserved GPUs, isolation needs, burst strategy and scaling. Customer evaluates hosted vs dedicated vs private, leaning toward Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation. They asked about burst/overflow to hosted, autoscale behaviors, network/VPC setup, KMS, and procurement cadence.

Topics: Dedicated sizing, burst policy, SLA and uptime targets, isolation (tenancy/data), security controls (KMS, audit logs, SSO), benchmark plan, pricing commit length, hardware options (A100/H100), autoscaling and warm pools, canary/rollout options.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Rafael and Lina joining from solutions. Hey Sara, Tom, Priya, Alex, thanks for your time.
[00:12] Sara: Hi thanks y'all, quick context, we run a couple of customer-facing LLM features — chat, summarize, and some doc search embeddings. Latency matters for chat, cost matters for embeddings at scale. We're evaluating options: hosted to get up fast, dedicated for predictability and isolation, private only if we need on-prem.
[00:30] Rafael: Great. Can you share rough qps and model mix? That helps us size Dedicated pools.
[00:40] Tom: Sure, right now in prod we see peaks of around 60 rps for chat endpoints, avg payload 256 tokens, peaks up to 512. Embeddings are batch jobs overnight, roughly 50k docs/day, some realtime embedding for search at 5-10 rps. We're planning growth ~2x over next 6 months.
[01:10] Priya: Important bit is that PII data cannot leave our VPC. We need network isolation and customer-managed KMS for key control. Also, procurement prefers a committed monthly spend for reserved GPUs.
[01:25] Lina: Okay, good. So Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in a VPC-connected deployment — we support customer-managed KMS and private networking for Dedicated or Private. A few clarifications: when you say "cannot leave VPC", do you mean fully air-gapped or just network egress controls?
[01:40] Priya: Network egress controls. We want strict peering and no public egress. Audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:50] Alex: Also need SOC 2 Type II evidence and subprocessor list. Encryption at rest and in transit must be enforced.
[02:05] Maya: Totally, we can share SOC2 and ISO artifacts. For Dedicated we can enable customer KMS for model artifacts and token logs, and our control plane can be configured for VPC peering. Logs can be forwarded to your Splunk/Datadog — we have audit forwarding.
[02:20] Sara: What's the typical commit size for Dedicated? We want to understand minimums and burst allowances.
[02:28] Rafael: Typical contracts start at 4-8 GPUs for smaller pilots, 8-64 GPUs for mid-market. Commit terms vary — monthly or annual — and pricing improves with longer commits. We also support burst/overflow to hosted during spikes if you want that hybrid pattern.
[02:45] Tom: How does burst work? Is it automatic? Does it breach isolation?
[02:52] Rafael: Burst is policy-driven. You can set a priority: keep within Dedicated, then overflow to Redwood Hosted or to a cheaper model variant. For strict isolation customers we do a "no burst" policy — nothing leaves your dedicated pool or VPC. For others, we allow overflow but data sent to hosted is redacted or uses a model variant with no logs retained — there's some nuance, and we can document those options.
[03:20] Priya: That overflow to hosted sounds risky. We prefer reserved with local burst capacity — e.g., warm pool or pre-warmed standbys. Can Redwood do warm pools?
[03:30] Lina: Yes, we have warm pool capabilities and pre-warmed instances that sit idle to absorb short spikes; costed as a smaller reserve. For sustained bursts we recommend autoscaling policies with a buffer and scheduled scale-ups tied to expected traffic patterns.
[03:50] Maya: Also we support fast cold-start optimizations and KV cache warmups for common prompts, so bursts that reuse prefixes can be quick.
[03:58] Sara: Good to know. What about hardware choices — A100 vs H100 — and quantization tradeoffs?
[04:05] Rafael: We support both families. H100 gives better throughput for larger context and FP16/AMP. For cost efficiency, int8 or 4-bit quantization profiles are available for many open models; Redwood Optimize will suggest quant+model pairings based on your workload. There can be a small quality delta; we'll run evals on your prompt set.
[04:30] Tom: For our SLA, p99 latency should be under 600ms for the chat 256-token payload. Is that realistic on Dedicated?
[04:40] Rafael: Yes, for a Dedicated pool sized appropriately (we'd likely recommend 8x H100 or equivalent config depending on concurrency), 600ms p99 is achievable. We'll need to run benchmarks — different models and sequence lengths change kernel selection and latency.
[05:00] Priya: Let's talk about autoscaling. We need predictable billing and an upper bound on cost. How do you handle auto-scale to avoid runaway costs?
[05:10] Lina: Autoscaling is policy-based with a budget cap and cooldowns. You define min and max pool sizes and budget thresholds. We also support scheduled scaling for predictable patterns and can set hard caps to prevent exceeding committed spend.
[05:25] Maya: Another pattern is reserve a baseline and enable burst but with explicit alerts and approval for sustained capacity increases. That way procurement gets notified before big spend events.
[05:35] Alex: On the compliance front, can we bring our own HSM? We use an HSM-backed KMS.
[05:42] Rafael: Yes, BYOK via HSM/KMS integration is supported for Private and for some Dedicated configurations; we will validate the flow and share the integration doc. There are some operational steps for key rotation we should align on.
[05:55] Sara: What about tenancy — is Dedicated multi-tenant on hardware or single-tenant? We need to know for regulatory reasons.
[06:05] Lina: Dedicated is single-tenant at the GPU pool level for compute, meaning your workloads don't share the same GPUs with other customers. Control plane may be multi-tenant unless you opt for a Private deployment. We can also provide additional hardening like node isolation and no-swap kernels.
[06:25] Tom: Can you walk through a typical onboarding timeline?
[06:30] Maya: Pilot usually takes 2-4 weeks: provisioning test pool, run benchmarks, integrate VPC peering and KMS, run samples. Production rollout 4-8 weeks depending on procurement and infra readiness. If you choose annual commit we can accelerate provisioning.
[06:45] Priya: Procurement will need a SOW and clear cancellation terms. Also pricing: do you price per GPU-hour or per vCPU?
[06:53] Rafael: We price primarily per-GPU-hour for Dedicated plus a platform fee for support and console features. We also provide a projected monthly cost per the expected utilization. There are discounts for higher commits. Bursting to hosted has separate usage billing. We'll send a worksheet that breaks down cost by GPU type and expected utilization.
[07:10] Sara: For benchmarking, we want Redwood to run our prompt set against dedicated pool and against hosted to compare latency/cost. Can you do that?
[07:18] Rafael: Absolutely. We'll need a sanitized prompt set and expected concurrency pattern. We'll run p95/p99 latency, throughput, and cost per token. We'll provide a report with kernel selection notes and recommended quant profiles.
[07:30] Tom: On rollback and degradation — if a node fails, what are the SLA behaviors? We need failover strategies.
[07:38] Lina: We have redundancy across availability zones and automatic routing to other nodes in the pool. For critical SLAs you can enable cross-region fallback and automatic model variant fallback to keep responses consistent. We also support canary rollouts and automatic rollback on regression.
[07:55] Priya: Any limitations around model licensing? Are we allowed to host third-party proprietary models?
[08:02] Maya: We support customer-provided models, subject to export controls and some licensing constraints. We also curate open models and have verified variants. For proprietary models we do a review during onboarding.
[08:15] Alex: Do you have penetration testing reports and do you allow ATO-style assessments?
[08:21] Rafael: We can share pen-test summaries and support customer security assessments. For deeper ATO engagements we coordinate with our security team.
[08:32] Sara: Pricing ballpark for 16 GPUs H100? Just to set expectations.
[08:38] Rafael: Ballpark varies by region and term; for a 12-month commit the per-GPU price can be 30-45% lower than on-demand hosted equivalent. I'll avoid exact numbers on the call but will include detailed numbers in the worksheet.
[08:55] Tom: Ok that's fair. How do you handle logs and telemetry — can we disable chat logs or redact PII?
[09:03] Lina: Yes, logs retention and redaction policies are configurable. You can turn off request/response retention in Dedicated, or route logs to your SIEM and set retention there. For redaction we have built-in PII masking and can do token-level redaction hooks.
[09:20] Priya: Great. A couple more nitty-gritty items: network egress IPs for allowlist, support windows for maintenance, and the SLA uptime number.
[09:30] Maya: We'll provide maintenance windows and static egress ranges for allowlist. SLA target for Dedicated is typically 99.9% with credits — details in the SLA doc.
[09:40] Alex: For encryption in transit, do you use mTLS?
[09:44] Rafael: Yes, we support mTLS for service-to-service and TLS 1.3 for endpoints. Customer-managed certificates are possible too.
[09:52] Sara: Any integration hooks into our feature flags for canarying model changes?
[09:56] Lina: Redwood Console supports routing per-route, canary rollouts, and percentage-based traffic splits. You can bind routes to models and use automatic fallback rules.
[10:06] Tom: Will we be able to pin to a model version and rollback quickly?
[10:09] Rafael: Yes, model versioning is supported, and rollbacks can be done via Console or API. We recommend versioned deployments and canary policy templates.
[10:20] Maya: Quick recap and proposed next steps: we'll send the Dedicated pricing worksheet, SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration guide, Rafael will prepare a benchmark template, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive with Priya and Tom next week to validate VPC/KMS flow.
[10:37] Priya: Sounds good. Procurement will want the SOW and payment terms up front.
[10:42] Maya: Understood. We'll include a draft SOW with cancellation terms in the packet.
[10:50] Sara: Timeline-wise we aim to decide by end of month, pilot in mid-April if procurement and infra align.
[10:57] Maya: Great. Rafael, Lina — anything to add?
[11:00] Rafael: I'll note we need the prompt set and sample traffic profile. Also, if you have a preference for GPU type say so, but we'll recommend based on latency/cost tradeoffs after initial run.
[11:12] Lina: We'll include options for warm pools and exact autoscale policies in the worksheet.
[11:20] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[11:22] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling invites.

End of call.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hears and shorthand from the call (e.g., "K-V cash" heard instead of KV cache in one snippet). There was standard vendor-QA interruptions. Customer prioritized VPC/KMS, commit pricing, and burst strategy.
